TextBlock.Text: Commander Rules
Northern Fleet Command

In June 1985 the Soviet Northern Fleet deployed a surface strike group into the Norwegian Sea and North Atlantic. You command that force — a task force of Soviet Navy surface combatants, submarines, and aviation assets operating far from home ports against NATO naval power.
Your commander is Soviet. Commander nationality does not change mission rules, ship performance, aircraft performance, or combat capability.
National Purchase Discount

Run.Text: % point discount when purchasing units from their own nation.

TextBlock.Text: - All available units in this campaign are Soviet, so the discount applies across the entire roster.
Awards and Promotions
- Your commander's campaign progress is tracked in the Service Record.
- The Service Record includes promotions, medals, total kills, losses, survivors rescued, and score.
- Completing key missions earns rank promotions. Reach the final mission to achieve the highest distinction.
- Select an award or ribbon to read its full citation.
Task Force Rules
Building Your Task Force
- Before each mission, use the Task Force Builder to purchase ships, submarines, aircraft, and helicopters within your available point budget.
- At least one surface ship must be in your task force before you can deploy.
- Submarines operate in separate optional side missions. They do not appear alongside your surface task force.
Points and Costs
- Each unit in your roster has a point cost. Your available points are shared across all units in the task force.
- Mission completion earns campaign points. Points accumulate up to the cap across the campaign.
- Repairing damaged ships costs points. Manage your budget carefully — a depleted treasury limits what you can deploy on the next mission.
Crew Experience
- Crew experience improves as ships survive missions and accumulate engagement time.
- More experienced crews react faster, aim more accurately, and are harder to suppress in combat.
- Losing veteran ships is a serious setback. Protect high-experience units where possible.
Air Tasking

- Aircraft squadrons assigned to land bases can be pre-tasked before a mission launches. Open Prepare Airbase from the selected mission and use the Air Tasking tab to assign eligible unassigned aircraft before launch.
- Each Air Tasking row represents one mission flight. Larger flights must use the same aircraft type, but may launch partially filled if too few aircraft are available.
- Submarines operate independently of your task force. They appear in separate optional side missions, which offer benefits to complete, but do not advance the main campaign.
- A surface ship is required before the task force can deploy.
- The first ship in your task force is the flagship by default. You can assign any ship as flagship from Task Force Manager.
- The flagship must survive each mission. Other units in the task force may be lost, but if the flagship is destroyed, the mission fails.
Search and Rescue
- Life rafts may appear when ships are sunk or aircraft are shot down. Move a helicopter or ship close to the rafts to recover survivors.

Run.Text: survivors rescued in a mission awards 1 campaign point at mission end. Partial groups do not award additional points.

TextBlock.Text: Mission Outcomes
- Losing a mission does not damage your task force or apply additional penalties.
- A failed mission must be replayed and completed successfully to advance.
- Completed missions can be replayed with the original task force built for that mission.
- After completing the campaign, all missions unlock for use with any task force you configure.
Unit Prices
Review available unit classes and point costs. Select a class name to open its unit reference. Use the Task Force Builder to add units to your task force.
